title: Brown's work in the B-2 and Floyd Odlum's funding

tellings.quote: In fact, Floyd Odlam, who is the majority owner of Northrup, who funded Brown's work in the 60s, paid Brown 4,000 bucks or I don't remember, 2,000 bucks 4,000 bucks a month, his family uh uh the same amount uh until until he died.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Floyd Odlum, whom he calls the majority owner of the aircraft maker Northrop, paid for the work of Townsend Brown, an American inventor who experimented with high voltage and gravity, starting in the 1960s. According to Michels, Odlum paid Brown a monthly sum, something like two to four thousand dollars, and kept paying his family the same until he died. Michels links this to Brown's work feeding into the B-2, a later American stealth bomber, which if true would tie Brown's odd experiments to a real military aircraft.
